notes.title: Patch 1.2.4 Notes
notes.content:
Howdy! Here’s a small patch coming your way. Don’t worry - we’re still hard at work behind the scenes getting everything ready for that exciting news we teased back in March. Stay tuned!

Changes:

 The Employee Introduction Video (shown when starting a new game) used to be lovingly mixed by one of our programmers. Now that our amazing sound and music producer, Simon Scholz, has joined us full-time, it’s received a full audio makeover. Check it out!
 Some players weren’t fans of the camera’s up-and-down motion. We’ve heard you! You can now disable that movement in the settings.

As always, thank you for playing American Cooking Simulator!

notes.title: Patch 1.2.3 Notes
notes.content:
Howdy! It's been a bit. We've made some additional changes due to feedback and bug reports we've received.

Bugfixes:

 Fixed bug where the assembly box could collect ingredients even if it was closed.
 Fixed bug where the "Perfect Candidate!" achievement was triggered even if only four shifts had an S rank.
 Fixed bug where an ingredient could be reported as raw and burnt in the same time during the rating.
 Adjusted table colliders to prevent boxes getting stuck.

Changes:

 Added an eating VFX for rats.
 Decreased the ingredient detector size for rats.


Besides that, we also did a lot of code cleanup - something you'll never get to see, but very important for us! Especially since we have some exciting news... 
If you remember from our release post, we talked about how we're not sure yet whether American Cooking Simulator will get content updates in the future. We can now confidently say that it will, and that quite soon! Stay tuned for more details coming around April, and thank you for playing American Cooking Simulator!

notes.title: Patch 1.2.2 Notes
notes.content:
New patch incoming! This time, less bugfixing and more fixing some gameplay aspects. It has been a blast (pun intended) watching people on YouTube play the game, but it also showed us some common issues. With this update we'd like to fix some of them.

Bugfixes:

 Previously, the "Not bad for a rookie!" wouldn't be triggered even if you finished the first shift. This has been fixed now and if you've already played through the game, you can just select level 1 in the level selection again, no need to restart completely. 


Changes:

 We've noticed that a lot of people thought a burnt patty was cooked. To combat this, we not only changed the texture of the burnt patty to be, hopefully, unmistakenly burnt, but we've also enabled the Joe Hannes voiceline event in the tutorial for this.
 Additionally, a lot of players don't realize that you can shoot at the yellow target above the conveyor belt claws in order for ingredients to fall straight down. To combat this, we've changed the texture to make the target more clear.
 Another problem with our tutorial that we've noticed was that a lot of players think you need to assemble a whole burger. Since we wanted to keep it as simple as possible, we only want the player to deliver a patty, so in order to make that more clear, we've adjusted the position of the red arrow to point at the TV now, as well as removing all buns from the tutorial shift.
 The Quit button in the In-Game-Menu has been replaced with a Restart button.
 The Weapon and Chef's Eye Reminder voicelines now get triggered much later; previously it was at 20 seconds (of not switching weapons) and 30 seconds (of not using Chef's Eye), now it's at 40 and 50 seconds respectively. Also for those who didn't know, if these two particular voicelines annoy you, you can turn them off by toggling the Tooltip setting in the In-Game-Menu!
 The Shotgun cooldown has been changed from 1 second to 0.85 seconds.

notes.title: Patch 1.2.1 Notes
notes.content:
Bugixes:

 Fixed bug that caused rats to be unable to be shot out of assembly boxes.
 Fixed bug that gave the player penalties for placing more than two cucumber or tomato slices on a burger that required it. It was always intended to place between two and four on a burger without getting a penalty for it.

Additionally, we've now added a version number in the main menu.

notes.title: Patch 1.1 Notes
notes.content:
Howdy! Thanks to everyone who already downloaded and played American Cooking Simulator so far. We've fixed two issues that came with the release version:


 The bug that sometimes caused the player being unable to shoot with the pistol and the AR has been fixed.
 The volume of the introduction video has been adjusted.

If you find any other issues, please reach out to us, either over the forum or via our email: americancookingsimulator@gmail.com

notes.title: American Cooking Simulator - Now available!
notes.content:
Yeehaw, it's Release Day!
Check out our trailer to get a look at what you can expect from this game:

[previewyoutube=4zv1_D7OQ3g;full][/previewyoutube]

What is American Cooking Simulator about?

American Cooking Simulator is a combination of a First Person Shooter and a Cooking Simulator - as an underpaid employee in training at Joe's Freedom Burgers, your job is to prepare burgers and deliver them to your customers. But this is America, so of course your only kitchen utensils are firearms. Good luck trying to figure out how to cook with those! 

After each shift, you will be rated for your performance, which determines whether you will be hired by the end of the week. And to add to the pressure, your boss Joe Hannes will scream at you for any mistakes you make in the kitchen, so better be fast, efficient and precise, no matter how chaotic the kitchen gets!

What's next?

Some background first of all: American Cooking Simulator is a student project which was developed from October 2024 up until now, February 2025 (that is, if you don't count in the very first prototype that was created during the GGJ 2024!). That means we are operating on a negative budget (since the game is free, but we still had to pay the Steam fee, of course), and since we are not taking money for the game, it is not feasible for any of us to continue working on it as we need to continue with our studies. Therefore, while we will of course take care of major bugs or issues you might encounter, but please do not expect any major content updates.

However.

There is a possibility that American Cooking Simulator can be developed for the length of another semester in the context of our studies. If that happens, there will definitely be major updates throughout the course of April until approximately August. But we currently cannot guarantee that this will happen, so for now, we hope you like the game as it is! We will update you at the beginning of April when we know more.

Thank you!

For now, we want to sincerely thank everyone who's already wishlisted ACS so far, we never expected to gain so much traction with our silly little student project! We hope we can live up to your expectations and that you'll enjoy the game as much as we enjoyed making it. If you encounter any major bugs or issues, please don't be afraid to write an email to us via americancookingsimulator@gmail.com

Now get out there and cook some burgers!
